body:
Hello, I want to propose a small feature to the [`MiniPick.default_choose_marked()`](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/9d359222b3643f1fccbd8f3180445842e1cae00b/lua/mini/pick.lua#L1186) so the user can control the quickfix/location list position and height/width.

## Reasoning

### copen behavior

Sometimes, `:copen`'s split behavior is not desired by the user.
For example, at a vertical split `:copen` will open below the last created window instead of the current window.

```text
---------                ---------               ---------
|       |                |   |   |               |   |   |
|       |                |   |   |               |   | B |
|   A   |  =`:vsplit`=>  | A | B |  =`:copen`=>  | A |---|
|       |                |   |   |               |   |QF |
|       |                |   |   |               |   |   |
---------                ---------               ---------
(The user create a new vertical split "B", move the cursor back to "A" and then call `:copen`, but the quickfix open below "B")
```

#### Vim solution to this problem

Vim solve this problem by letting the user combine `:copen`/`:lopen` with commands like `:vertical`, `:horizontal` and more (the full list of commands start with the tag `:h vertical` up to `:h botright` in the `:h windows.txt` file). It's even possible to combine multiple of those commands, like: `:vertical topleft copen 120` (Open a vertical split at the left occupying the full height and width equals 120).

### Current limitations using MiniPick.default_choose_marked()

It's not possible to specify the height before opening the quickfix/location list (It's possible to change the height after opened using an autocmd/filetype config).
The window position is always the default behavior of `:copen`/`:lopen`.

## Solution

> I know that is possible to override `source.choose_marked` with a user written function, but the burden of maintaining a identical function to `MiniPick.default_choose_marked()` is greater than a 3 lines of code change I want to propose.

Extend the `opts` parameter in `MiniPick.default_choose_marked()` so it accepts two more fields. One for the split behavior, and other for the width/height modifier.

Since `copen` and `lopen` are called only once in the codebase, the following changes suffice:

> `split` and `width_or_height` are just a naming suggestion.
> The example does not include changes in the documentation.
> The `tostring()` calls are totally optional since `string.format('%s', 2)` will return `"2"` (as a string type).
```lua
-- From line 1189
opts = vim.tbl_deep_extend('force', { list_type = 'quickfix' }, opts or {})
-- To
opts = vim.tbl_deep_extend('force', { list_type = 'quickfix', split = '', width_or_height = ''}, opts or {})

-- and

-- From line 1225
vim.schedule(function() vim.cmd('lopen') end)
-- To
vim.schedule(function() vim.cmd(string.format('%s lopen %s', opts.split, tostring(opts.width_or_height))) end)

-- From line 1228
vim.schedule(function() vim.cmd('copen') end)
-- To
vim.schedule(function() vim.cmd(string.format('%s copen %s', opts.split, tostring(opts.width_or_height)))
```

Code usage (user side) comparison:

> In the default case (`require('mini.pick').setup()`) there is no change in behavior and code.
```lua
-- Actual
local minipick = require('mini.pick')
minipick.setup({
    source = {
        choose_marked = function(items)
            minipick.default_choose_marked(items, { list_type = 'quickfix' })
        end
      }
  })

-- After changes

-- Make `quickfix` appears always at the bottom in any window layout, like:
-- ---------
-- |   | B |
-- | A |---|
-- |   | C |
-- ---------
-- |  QF   |
-- ---------

local minipick = require('mini.pick')
minipick.setup({
    source = {
        choose_marked = function(items)
            local len = math.min(#items, 5) -- Prevent split to get over 5 lines
            minipick.default_choose_marked(items, { list_type = 'quickfix', split = 'botright', width_or_height = len })
        end
      }
  })
```

I have tested the proposed solution locally without any issues.
Let me know what you think, and thanks for your time.

Hello, I want to propose a small feature to the MiniPick.default_choose_marked() so the user can control the quickfix/location list position and height/width.

Reasoning

copen behavior

Sometimes, :copen's split behavior is not desired by the user.
For example, at a vertical split :copen will open below the last created window instead of the current window.

---------                ---------               ---------
|       |                |   |   |               |   |   |
|       |                |   |   |               |   | B |
|   A   |  =`:vsplit`=>  | A | B |  =`:copen`=>  | A |---|
|       |                |   |   |               |   |QF |
|       |                |   |   |               |   |   |
---------                ---------               ---------
(The user create a new vertical split "B", move the cursor back to "A" and then call `:copen`, but the quickfix open below "B")

Vim solution to this problem

Vim solve this problem by letting the user combine :copen/:lopen with commands like :vertical, :horizontal and more (the full list of commands start with the tag :h vertical up to :h botright in the :h windows.txt file). It's even possible to combine multiple of those commands, like: :vertical topleft copen 120 (Open a vertical split at the left occupying the full height and width equals 120).

Current limitations using MiniPick.default_choose_marked()

It's not possible to specify the height before opening the quickfix/location list (It's possible to change the height after opened using an autocmd/filetype config).
The window position is always the default behavior of :copen/:lopen.

Solution

I know that is possible to override source.choose_marked with a user written function, but the burden of maintaining a identical function to MiniPick.default_choose_marked() is greater than a 3 lines of code change I want to propose.

Extend the opts parameter in MiniPick.default_choose_marked() so it accepts two more fields. One for the split behavior, and other for the width/height modifier.

Since copen and lopen are called only once in the codebase, the following changes suffice:

split and width_or_height are just a naming suggestion.
The example does not include changes in the documentation.
The tostring() calls are totally optional since string.format('%s', 2) will return "2" (as a string type).

-- From line 1189
opts = vim.tbl_deep_extend('force', { list_type = 'quickfix' }, opts or {})
-- To
opts = vim.tbl_deep_extend('force', { list_type = 'quickfix', split = '', width_or_height = ''}, opts or {})

-- and

-- From line 1225
vim.schedule(function() vim.cmd('lopen') end)
-- To
vim.schedule(function() vim.cmd(string.format('%s lopen %s', opts.split, tostring(opts.width_or_height))) end)

-- From line 1228
vim.schedule(function() vim.cmd('copen') end)
-- To
vim.schedule(function() vim.cmd(string.format('%s copen %s', opts.split, tostring(opts.width_or_height)))

Code usage (user side) comparison:

In the default case (require('mini.pick').setup()) there is no change in behavior and code.

-- Actual
local minipick = require('mini.pick')
minipick.setup({
    source = {
        choose_marked = function(items)
            minipick.default_choose_marked(items, { list_type = 'quickfix' })
        end
      }
  })

-- After changes

-- Make `quickfix` appears always at the bottom in any window layout, like:
-- ---------
-- |   | B |
-- | A |---|
-- |   | C |
-- ---------
-- |  QF   |
-- ---------

local minipick = require('mini.pick')
minipick.setup({
    source = {
        choose_marked = function(items)
            local len = math.min(#items, 5) -- Prevent split to get over 5 lines
            minipick.default_choose_marked(items, { list_type = 'quickfix', split = 'botright', width_or_height = len })
        end
      }
  })

I have tested the proposed solution locally without any issues.
Let me know what you think, and thanks for your time.

comment_data.body:
Hi @felpafel,

I read your post with interest. Thanks!

> Sometimes, :copen's split behavior is not desired by the user.
> For example, at a vertical split :copen will open below the last created window instead of the current window.

I can't reproduce that behavior using nightly. I tried with [MiniMax](https://github.com/nvim-mini/MiniMax), and also with an "empty" init.lua. The quickfix always opens below, occupying the full width.

> I know that is possible to override source.choose_marked with a user written function, but the burden of maintaining a identical function to MiniPick.default_choose_marked() is greater than a 3 lines of code change I want to propose.

You are comparing maintenance by users versus maintenance by the mini.nvim team. Also, by allowing the user to override `choose_marked`, the user obtains much more flexibility in customizing the behavior.

Perhaps it is a bit too much to have both the override and the configuration options.

Hello @abeldekat, thanks for the response.

Yeah, Nightly changed the default behavior compared to nvim stable and vim, but the window modifiers like `:vertical copen 120` are still valid, and useful. My point is just: "The user may want to open the qf window in another position and/or size".


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/647c7a40-4bc5-4270-8aba-09260c2b69dc

> Perhaps it is a bit too much to have both the override and the configuration options.

I didn't understand what you mean. The ability to override and the configuration options are already implemented, for example to send marked items to the location list (instead of the quickfix list) the user must do:

```lua
local minipick = require('mini.pick')
minipick.setup({
    source = {
        choose_marked = function(items)
            minipick.default_choose_marked(items, { list_type = 'location' })
        end
      }
  })
```

My issue is that the function call `:copen`/`:lopen` making it impossible to change the qf window position and size. And, from my understanding, the current solution is copying the `default_choose_marked` source code (with the helper functions used by it) to my config.

reply_data.body:
> My issue is that the function call :copen/:lopen making it impossible to change the qf window position and size

It is possible though:

```lua
---@diagnostic disable: undefined-global
vim.pack.add({ "https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim" })

require("mini.pick").setup({
  source = {
    choose_marked = function(items)
      MiniPick.default_choose_marked(items)
      vim.schedule(function()
        if vim.bo.filetype ~= "qf" then return end

        vim.cmd("resize " .. math.min(#items, 5))
      end)
    end,
  },
})
```

You can apply 'window' commands to the quickfix.

Edit:

> Perhaps it is a bit too much to have both the override and the configuration options.

That possibility is also why I made the comment quoted above. If the user can do a lot in an overridden function, the configuration options you propose are somewhat redundant.

reply_data.body:
I don't want to create a back and forward of replies (or to be rude), but in more complicated layouts this "hack" solutions will not work easily. For example:

The user cursor is at "B" then `:copen` is called , creating the layout in figure 1. To programmatically change it to the layout in figure 2 is a really hard work (I don't even know if there is a way to query the current window layout and transverse it with ease). In comparison, a simple `:vertical copen width` will do the job.

```text
      (1)                              (2)
---------------                  ---------------
|   |    B    |                  |   |  B | QF |
| A |---------|                  | A |---------|
|   |    C    |                  |   |         |
|-------------|                  |   |    C    |
|     QF      |                  |   |         |
---------------                  ---------------
```

I'm not arguing that my solution is the only solution and I know that my example is "silly", I'm just trying to pass my point, that is, for me to change how `:copen` is called in `default_choose_marked()` I have to roll my on `H.parse_item`, `H.parse_item_*` and other help functions.

Another solution that came to my mind is to MiniPick to have a `toqflist()`¹ (Similar to the `vim.diagnostic.toqflist()`) so the user is free to do whatever they want with it.

¹ The code for the `toqflist()` already exists [here](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/9990c41f10f54f29a888d13024c9f765037bde23/lua/mini/pick.lua#L1192-L1202)

Again, thanks for participating in this discussion.

reply_data.body:
`:vertical copen 30`
`:copen`

It should jump to the already opened `:copen` window. All you need to do is manually create a window before the action.

P.S. I just don't feel like passing modifiers is the best solution, since the real problem is that the default functions are too smart and rely on hidden APIs, making them difficult to simply copy/paste or use as building blocks for other code.

I see that @echasnovski posted a better solution.

Just for the record, finishing my thoughts...)

As previously said, there is no good way to predict if the items argument will be parsed to a valid qflist without implementing the

There is, see :h MiniPick.default_choose_marked

The following code provides a custom dedicated mapping to invoke default_choose_marked when the user knows that the quickfix will be invoked:

---@diagnostic disable: undefined-global
vim.pack.add({ "https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim" })

require("mini.pick").setup({
  mappings = {
    choose_marked_quickfix = {
      char = "<M-q>",
      -- According to :h MiniPick.default_choose_marked(), quickfix is opened if
      -- marked items contain at least a file or buffer
      func = function()
        local pick_error = function(msg) error("(mini.pick) " .. msg, 0) end

        local choose_marked_override = function(items)
          if #items == 0 then return end

          vim.cmd("vertical copen 30")
          MiniPick.default_choose_marked(items)
        end

        local ok, res = pcall(choose_marked_override, MiniPick.get_picker_matches().marked)
        if not ok then vim.schedule(function() pick_error("Error during choose marked quickfix:\n" .. res) end) end
        return not (ok and res)
      end,
    },
  },
})

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the suggestion!

As others noted, adding new configurations to any 'mini.nvim' module is usually a hard decision, but for 'mini.pick' it is especially so due to its size.

My initial reaction is that this *might* be reasonable for two reasons:
- The code change should indeed be rather small.
- There is a precedent for [`opts.default_split` in `help` built-in picker](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-pick.html#minipick.builtin.help).

My second reaction was that I don't think that 'mini.pick' has to even decide how to open quickfix/loclist. Is it reasonable for the user to have 'mini.pick' open quickfix/loclist *differently* than it is usually done? I think the answer is no. So the solution here should be to configure quickfix to always open as you'd prefer. For example, something like this should fix this problem:

```lua
local fix_quickfix = function(ev)
  local qf_data = vim.fn.getqflist({ qfbufnr = true, size = true, winid = true })
  if qf_data.qfbufnr ~= ev.buf then return end
  vim.api.nvim_win_call(qf_data.winid, function()
    vim.cmd('wincmd J')
    vim.api.nvim_win_set_height(0, math.min(qf_data.size, 5))
  end)
end
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('FileType', { pattern = 'qf', callback = fix_quickfix, desc = 'Fix quickfix' })
```

@felpafel, does this solve the issue for you?

reply_data.body:
> Is it reasonable for the user to have 'mini.pick' open quickfix/loclist differently than it is usually done?

Well, nvim nightly change the default behavior of `:copen` be in a split below the last opened window (Can be tested on nvim 0.11.6 and Vim) to always be `:botright copen`. There are arguments from both sides on what should be the behavior ([Vim thinks window should be opened below last window](https://github.com/vim/vim/issues/12501)), but I think this is a solved problem enabling a window modifier (`:vertical`, etc..).

There are other 2 solutions presented by me that are worth thinking. One is the solution in telescope.nvim where `setqflist` is decouple from `copen` so the user is able to override just the open action. The other solution is to expose the code that generate the qflist like `vim.diagnostic.toqflist()` so the user can set the qflist and open it be themselves.

> @felpafel, does this solve the issue for you?

Sadly, but no. There is a way to know if the qflist was set in the first place? (maybe `vim.schedule(function() if vim.bo.filetype == 'qf' then... end)`). Second, the code is "fine" to force `:botright` behavior, but sometimes I want to open vertically right relative to the current cursor position, with make it more trick (Since nightly put it on the `:botright` position). And on my machine, I can see the window being created on the default location and them moving to the `:botright` position.
